campaign.title: Licensing as a contract area: the product's licence stated once and carried everywhere
campaign.status: Phases 1, 2 and 3 landed on main; Phase 4 is done on both release branches of the pilot except its builds: surfaces, carriers, proofs and guard committed, each branch squashed to one commit, force-pushed to both remotes on the owner's yes, and the stale local history and old-posture copies deleted on the owner's second yes, insured by verified bundles in the owner's backup folder. Codkit: the design and plan; the contract area with its specifications; the editor family's answer; the engine - the profile and the surfaces, `gen licensing` with the header from the profile, `license annotate --own` with `--replace-retired`, the `verify` gate with its three codes, the notice naming the skill projections, the document exemption of PROP-006, the unconfigured-operation ruling of PROP-019, the human page 16 and the command reference. Still open: the portable Linux installer (DEF-8) and the macOS host, the mirroring and push of Codkit's own commits, the recreation of the pilot's GitHub repository (the owner's call), the owner review points RP-1..RP-4; Phase 5 deferred by name.

campaign.mandate-note: The mandate names the pilot consumer by its product name, elided here as [пилот]; this plan and the tool's texts call it the pilot (`common/PROP-004` `NO-CONSUMER-PRODUCT-IN-THE-TOOL`). The owner's earlier decisions of the same day that shape the pilot - a banner on every own file except the tool's, no second banner in modified upstream files, the canonical text in a Markdown licence file, an RTF for the installer - are recorded in the pilot's own repository and in DESIGN-003 §2.
campaign.source: DESIGN-003-licensing-area.md (vibevm/vibespecs/research/design), written 2026-11-01 from PROP-014, PROP-015, PROP-016 and PROP-019, the engine's licensing modules (`organizationPolicy`, `organizationPolicyStore`, `consumerLicenseCheck`, `releaseLicensing`, `distributionNotices`, `distributionDocuments`, `distributionProvenance`, `licenseCarrier`, `licenseAnnotate`, `genTemplates`, `genFeature`), the type contract (`packages/type-api`), the `vscode` type and the pilot's measured state.

baseline.fact: The contract has eleven areas and the closed capability list `brand-images, gen-brand, build-channels, runtime-library, own-extensions, service-override, entry-module, config-overlay, dev-channel, upgrade-advisory, preview`; `OPTIONAL_AREAS` pairs `brandImages`, `runtime` and `preview` with their capabilities (`packages/type-api/src/projectType.ts` on f3e8d8c).

PROP-019 is implemented except `ORGANIZATION-DISTRIBUTION-EVIDENCE` (spec/done): a trusted store, consumer source scanning (`license consumer-check`), release selection (`codkit.licensing.json` v1 with `package`/`publish` declarations), notice and provenance checks and NOTICE/SPDX rendering. `verify` never reads the selection; `gen` never reads the policy; `license annotate` serves the tool's packages.

`gen --header-style block` writes `Copyright (c) <year> <holder>. All rights reserved.` on one line; `COPYRIGHT_LINE` of `licenseCarrier.ts` takes everything after the year as the holder, so the consumer check reads a foreign holder (`DESIGN-003` §1.6). No test runs the two against each other.

`LICENSE-CODKIT.md` (`packages/codkit/config/`) names three path groups "and nowhere else"; `vibe skill install` projects the tool's skills with their UPL headers under `.claude/skills/ck-*`, `.agents/skills/ck-*` and `.opencode/skills/ck-*` of a consumer, which the notice does not list.

The pilot: 169 own files headed with a personal source-available notice; a static proof, a lint patch and a decision record mandating it; the built product shipping the upstream's licence text as its own, the installer showing it, the package manifest keeping the upstream's licence field, the notices silent about the tool's runtime; no `codkit.licensing.json`, no store on the machine (measured 2026-11-01 in the pilot's repository and fork tree).

Gates on f3e8d8c: format, typecheck, runtime emit, type receipts, trace, docs, public formats, `vibe check --quiet` green; the full Vitest suite is red on this machine on the untouched baseline (52 files, environment), so only focused suites count as evidence.

decisions.decision: Licensing is the twelfth area of the contract, optional, capability `licensing`, paired in `OPTIONAL_AREAS` (DESIGN-003 D1). Rejected: a type-specific verb; a `licence` layer.
The organization policy stays the single authority; `codkit.licensing.json` v2 adds a `product` block of display choices only (DESIGN-003 D2). Rejected: a policy format 3.
The header comes from the profile when one is selected; the flags must agree with it; the house form must resolve to a conforming carrier; without a profile nothing changes (DESIGN-003 D3).
The block header is laid out as a carrier the parser reads, with a test over both styles (DESIGN-003 D4).
`gen licensing` writes overlays, add-file patches, renderings and the guard from the profile and the type's answer; `--update` rewrites its own artifacts (DESIGN-003 D5).
`license annotate --own` gives own files their carriers in the family's style; `--replace-retired` replaces a foreign-holder header; resources are annotated by path only (DESIGN-003 D6).
`verify` is the gate: profile, source carriers, surfaces; `package`/`publish` refusal deferred (DESIGN-003 D7, DEF-3).
One guard template rendered by the engine with the type's runner words (DESIGN-003 D8).

Codkit-side work lands on `main` in atomic commits per phase, each with the floor pieces that run on this machine; the pilot's work lands in its own repository and is not a commit of this one. The tool's texts name no consumer, no holder and no legal entity.

predictions.prediction: After Phase 1, `projectTypeProblems` refuses a type that declares `licensing` without the area and one that answers the area without the capability, by the same test that holds `preview` today; `codkit types` prints the new capability name in the contract's list and no other change.

After Phase 2, a file headed by `gen --header-style block` from a profile passes `license consumer-check` as own; the same file headed by the pre-campaign block form is read as third-party - the unit test records both.

After Phase 2, on the stub fixture with a store in a temporary home: `gen licensing` writes the overlay operations for the stub's manifest fields, an add-file patch whose body is the policy's canonical text, the component licence of the fixture upstream and the guard; a second run is `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`; a run with `--update` after a changed canonical text rewrites exactly those artifacts and `verify` goes from one `LICENSE-SURFACE` finding to zero.

After Phase 2, `license annotate --own` over a fixture own layer with one headerless source, one JSON and one file headed by a foreign holder writes one header, one sidecar and, with `--replace-retired`, one replacement; a second run is all `unchanged`; `verify` with the profile reports zero `LICENSE-HEADER` findings.
After Phase 3, the `vscode` type declares `licensing` and `codkit types` prints it; the guard rendered for the family uses `suite`/`test`; the overlay target `package.json` admits the key `license`.

The pilot: both release trees, passed through the same commands, differ afterwards only where they differed before plus the licence surfaces; the fork tree grep for the retired notices prints zero outside the tool's notice; the guard is green under the product's own test run; the built installer shows the product's text and the application root carries the Markdown licence, the RTF and `licenses/` with the upstream's and the tool's texts.

route.phase: Measurement and design, no commits: the pilot's repository, fork tree, remotes, copies and build read; the engine's licensing modules read; DESIGN-003 written; this plan proposed. Complete 2026-11-01.

Contract and specifications: `licensing` capability and `LicensingArea` in `@codkit/type-api` with the shape rules; PROP-016 `TYPE-AREA-LICENSING` and the capability list; PROP-019 new facts; PROP-015 `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS` amended; PROP-007 `CMD-GEN-LICENSING`, the amended `CMD-LICENSE-ANNOTATE`, `CMD-VERIFY`, `CMD-GEN-FEATURE`, `CMD-GEN-BRAND` and the roster; PROP-012 codes; PROP-014 notice scope; FEAT-002 scenarios; `modules/vscode/PROP-010`; the stub type answers the area; specmap and docs regenerated. Exit: `vibe check --quiet`, specmap --check, trace:check, typecheck, docs:check green; the contract suite green.

The engine: `licensingProfile` (declaration v1/v2, profile selection, product block), the header from the profile in `gen feature|brand` and the block layout of D4 with the two-style carrier test, `genLicensing` (plan, overlay merge, add-file patches, RTF and text renderings, the guard template, `--update`), `license annotate --own` (walk, styles, sidecars, `--replace-retired`), `verify`'s licensing check and the two codes with FAQ entries, `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` and the printed recommendation naming the skill projections; unit and e2e suites on the stub fixture with a store in a temporary home. Exit: the focused suites green, P2-P4 recorded, docs regenerated, the floor pieces green.

The editor family: `packages/type-vscode/src/licensing.ts`, the capability in the manifest and the registry receipts, the `license` key of the `package.json` overlay target, the type's suite; `modules/vscode/PROP-003` and `PROP-010` to impl/done. Exit: the type's suites green, `codkit types` prints the capability, P5 recorded.

The pilot: the profile in the machine store, `codkit.licensing.json` v2, `gen licensing`, `license annotate --own --replace-retired`, the pilot's own proofs turned around, `verify` to zero, `load --fresh`, a build, the acceptance checks, on both release trees; then the squash the owner decided. The proof is reported in the pilot's repository; this plan records only that the area passed it.

The extension family's answer; the application family's answer; `package`/`publish` refusal on incomplete evidence with a build mapping from the family's bundler; the NOTICE section of modified upstream files; REUSE annotations as an alternative to sidecars for directories of data files; the bootstrap rule of the standards (a declared rights holder before the first `gen`).

review-points.point: Owner-only: one RTF of the whole text at the root, or one per installer language under `licenses/`. Conservative reading applied: one at the root.
Owner-only: whether the tool's licence text is shipped under `licenses/` as a component licence. Conservative reading applied: shipped, because the runtime library is delivered into the product.
Owner-only: the year of headers, fixed in the product block or the year of generation. Conservative reading applied: fixed in the product block when given, else the year of generation.

A newer edition of the tool's notice meets copies written by the previous edition in every consumer: `standards load` and `runtime load` refuse the drift, their hint names `--upgrade` first, and `--upgrade` does not take a notice copy (the unit test "keeps refusing an edited notice copy even with the flag" fixes that choice). The documented recovery works - delete both copies, run `standards load` - and the pilot used it. Question for the owner: should `--upgrade` take drifted notice copies as it takes a drifted package, or should the drift hint stop naming the flag for the notice? The campaign changes nothing here.

quick-start.step: Read DESIGN-003 and this plan; `git log --oneline -5` on main; `node packages/codkit/bin/codkit.mjs types`.

Phase 1 starts in `packages/type-api/src/` (add `licensing.ts`, extend `capabilities.ts`, `OPTIONAL_AREAS`, `projectTypeProblems`, `index.ts`) and in the specifications named above; regenerate `specmap.json` with `vibe bin exec --quiet typescript-ai-native -- specmap` and the docs with `node tools/generate-codkit-docs.mjs`.

Gates per boundary: `npm run format:check && npm run typecheck && npm run runtime:build && npm run runtime:check && npm run types:check && npm run trace:check && npm run docs:check && npm run formats:check && vibe check --quiet && vibe bin exec --quiet typescript-ai-native -- specmap --check`, plus the Vitest files the phase touched.

deferrals.deferral: The extension family's and the application family's answers to the area (DESIGN-003 D11).
The NOTICE section listing modified upstream files, rendered from the inventory (DESIGN-003 D9).
`package`/`publish` refusal on incomplete licensing evidence (`ORGANIZATION-DISTRIBUTION-EVIDENCE`), which needs a build mapping from the family's bundler (DESIGN-003 D7).

REUSE annotations for directories of data files as an alternative to one sidecar per file. Resolved in Phase 2: `license annotate --own` honours the registries of the own layers as the consumer check does (an own annotation covers its files without a sidecar, a `third-party;` annotation keeps a derived directory untouched), the guard reads the nearest registry inside the scope, and `verify` accepts the annotation carrier - PROP-019 `ANNOTATE-OWN`, `LICENCE-GUARD`.
A standards rule and a skill note that a product declares its rights holder before its first `gen`, and that a placeholder posture is recorded with an expiry.

REUSE precedence in the carrier model: a third party's source file whose header carries a copyright line but no `SPDX-License-Identifier`, under an `aggregate` annotation that names the licence, is read today as a header carrier that lacks its SPDX line (`consumer carrier requires copyright and exactly one SPDX expression`); REUSE combines the file's own information with the annotation (`aggregate`), takes the file's when it is complete (`closest`) and the annotation's when it says so (`override`). The carrier selection, the consumer check, `annotate --own` and the guard should follow those three rules together, with PROP-014 `LIC-CARRIER-ANNOTATION` saying so. Found on the pilot (vendored texts of a localisation pack); not blocking it, since licence texts are metadata (`LIC-UNSCANNED-SET`) and its data files carry no header.

Packaging the editor family on a Linux host that is not the upstream's build agent: the type routes a Linux target natively on a Linux host and its glibc check then fails on native modules compiled against the host's glibc (found on the pilot: Ubuntu 26.04, `spdlog.node` wants glibc 2.33, the check wants 2.28), while the type's own container route - the upstream build agent with its sysroots and Chromium clang - is taken only on other hosts. A way to ask for the container route on a Linux host, or a documented host recipe equal to the container's `entry.sh`, belongs to the packaging area, not to this campaign.

The guard scopes the owned roots of `delta/own-roots/**` (`layout.ownRoots` beyond the own root): one scope per owned root present in the patch set, its tree directory from the type's answer, its expression resolved for its delta directory, its `buildOutputs` skipped. `verify` and `license annotate --own` already treat the owned roots as own (`ownLayerPaths`); the guard, written to the text of `LICENCE-GUARD`, covers the own root and the own extensions. The editor family answers one owned directory, so no consumer of this campaign is affected; the application family, when it answers the area (DEF-1), needs this first.

log.entry: The owner said yes to the deletion, and the pilot's stale local history and old-posture copies went, insurance first. Insured in a dated folder of the owner's backup directory, every bundle verified before its source was removed: the pre-squash bundle of the patch set; a bundle of both stashes (one identical spec draft, also saved as a patch); full bundles of the two pilot copies that lived in the backup directory - their branch tips were in the repository's objects but reachable from no ref, so gc would have taken them; six thin bundles above the upstream pin for the fork-tree copies (three exports of the first release, a release-candidate clone and its tarred snapshot, an enterprise clone of the old generated branch); and a SHA-256 manifest of twelve deleted archives. Deleted: the three stale branches, both stashes, the archive and Codex checkpoint refs and the three worktrees of the patch set; the provisional cycle branch and the old-posture build worktree of the fork tree; twenty-three built bundles, seven unpacked and seven archived distributions of the first pilot version, the fork-tree copies and archives named above, the two backup copies - about 70 GB. Then the reflogs of both repositories expired and gc pruned them: the patch set from 7649 to 1781 objects with two reachable commits, the fork tree from 27 packs to one. Verified after: in the patch set the retired phrases survive only where they are named (the declaration's retired notices, the static proof's list, a risk-register row, the decision record, the licensing world package's texts); in the fork tree both generated branches stand regenerated today with the new posture (152 and 156 commits, no retired header, no banner), and the clean upstream-pin worktree of a job record stays. Finds beyond the inventory, left to the owner: the owner's build-tooling repository beside the pilot carries 410 files with the retired phrases; a copy of Codkit's pre-rewrite history and two Codkit backups stand beside the repository; the job-records folder (25 GB) was not scanned. The LFS stores of the two deleted clones held only the upstream's test caches.

The owner said yes to the force-push: the pilot's squashed `main`, `release/1.0.0`, `release/1.1.0` and the tag `1.0.0` were pushed with leases on the observed heads to both of its remotes (the release branches and the tag created, `main` moved from its old history); the old history is in the pre-squash bundle of the session. Still pending the owner's word: the deletion of stale local branches, stashes, worktrees and copies; the mirroring of Codkit's own commits; the portable Linux build (DEF-8) and the macOS host.

Phase 4, both release branches of the pilot done locally: release/1.1.0 (168 banners replaced) and release/1.0.0 (132), each with the same surfaces, registries, proofs and guard; on both `verify`, the static proof, the guard in the tree and the family's lint are clean, and the only leftovers of the retired phrases in the trees are the tool's own notices. Release/1.0.0 also took the current delivered runtime library (`runtime load --upgrade`; the drift was the dot-access rewrite of one file) and both branches took the current edition of the tool's notice by the documented path (RP-4). The owner moved the builds to their machines: Linux on `cloud`, macOS on `flash`. On `cloud` the pilot was set up from bundles (Codkit, the patch set, the documentation input - named in `codkit.local.json`), the upstream cloned from GitHub, `load --fresh` and `verify` passed, and the raw Linux bundle was built: its `product.json` names the EULA and its file and carries no licence URLs, its `package.json` names the EULA, `resources/app/LICENSE.md` is the canonical text, `licenses/` and `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` are there, and not one retired phrase survives in the bundle (the owner's name appears as the product owner in `vcodeTeam` of `product.json` and in the tool's UPL notice - product data and the tool's licence, not the retired posture). The installer target `linux-x64-tar` stopped at upstream's glibc check, because the host is not the upstream build agent (DEF-8); the macOS host has no node yet. Two engine findings on the way, both landed: `codkit package` refused a declaration without a `package` section (ffee93a), and a user-level npm setting (`allow-scripts`) broke the upstream's nested `npm ci` - a build-host matter, neutralised with `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`. Next: the squash of both branches to one commit each (the owner's ask), then the owner's separate yes for the force-push and for the deletion of the stale local branches, stashes, worktrees and copies.

Phase 4 begun on the first release branch of the pilot, and the pilot paid for itself at once. Codkit fixes it forced, all with tests: (1) the header form of a carrier belongs to a file with a comment style - the upstream's notice inside a translation file's JSON string had been read as a foreign header (PROP-014 `LIC-CARRIER-HEADER`); (2) the licence texts of REUSE (`LICENSE`, `LICENCE`, `COPYING` with or without one extension) are metadata, never carriers - a localisation pack's Microsoft MIT text had become a `LICENSE-HEADER` finding (`LIC-UNSCANNED-SET`, one rule shared by the package check and the consumer check); (3) the guard accepts a declared third party and applies the header window only to files with a comment style, with the engine's table of comment-style names baked in, and reads the manifest fields through the type's dev channel in a development tree (`LICENCE-GUARD`); (4) the guard passes the family's lint and hygiene - 162 warnings on the first render: every branch braced, every baked literal single-quoted and ASCII-only, the builtin modules by bare names, dot access to named groups, and a `preamble` the type answers for the lines its lint needs in front of the suite (PROP-016 `TYPE-AREA-LICENSING`, modules/vscode `VSCODE-LICENCE-GUARD`: the disposable-leak directive). Pilot-side fixes: the EULA text no longer says the retired phrase it forbade, the retired notices are the exact old lines (the tool's own holder is a person who must not be a retired phrase), three own files had stray CR bytes, the pilot's static proof and its sample code learnt the new posture. Result on release/1.1.0 (commit d6845a1 in the pilot): `verify` clean, static proof 1082/1082, the guard green in the tree and lint-clean, 168 banners replaced, no retired phrase in the own layers; the tree's leftovers are the tool's own notices. Then `codkit package` refused a declaration without a `package` section - DEF-3's payload provenance, which the licensing area never promised to write - and the ruling followed the facts: an operation the declaration leaves unconfigured runs, the trusted profile is its evidence and the notices, provenance and SBOM stay missing in a release recorded as incomplete (`LICENSING-DECLARATION-V2`); on the way, `verify` inside `publish` learnt to read the trusted store a programmatic caller names, and the publish fixture gained its surfaces and carriers, as every patch set that selects a profile now must. DEF-7 added (REUSE precedence for a third party's header without an SPDX line).

Phase 2 landed: the engine. The shared modules (`licensingProfile`, `licensingSurfaces`, `addFilePatch`, `pinBytes`, the carrier block of D4, `allowedScalarKeys`), `gen licensing` with the header from the profile, `license annotate --own` with `--replace-retired`, the `verify` gate with `LICENSE-PROFILE`/`LICENSE-HEADER`/`LICENSE-SURFACE`, the notice naming the skill projections, the human page 16 and the command reference. Three findings at integration, all fixed before the commit: (1) the REUSE annotation `standards license` prints claimed four paths while the notice claimed seven - the rows now list the notice's scope (D10 extended; `STD-LICENSE-PRINTS-REUSE-ROWS`, the decision's revisit clause); (2) the first `.md` licence file met `ADD-FILE-EXEMPTION`: `verify` demanded a marker block inside the licence text, which the same `verify` compares with the canonical text byte for byte - a surface is a document shipped verbatim, so `verify` (the full run and the staged check) and `save` now read the surfaces' add-file patches as block-free, their paths computed from the type's area and the declaration without the store (PROP-006 `LICENCE-DOCUMENT-EXEMPTION`); the defect surfaced only through the closing clause of S92, which no suite had carried end to end, and that clause is now an e2e case; (3) the annotate engine had copied the consumer check's two readers - they are exported and shared. Predictions: P2 held (S96: both own forms are carriers, the pre-campaign block is a foreign holder); P3 held end to end (S91/S92: write, refuse, `--update` after a new edition, and `verify` from one `LICENSE-SURFACE` to zero); P4 held (S93: header, sidecar, `foreign-holder`, `replaced`, all `unchanged` on the second run, `verify` with zero `LICENSE-HEADER`); P1 and P5 held in Phases 1 and 3. Gates: format, typecheck, runtime:build/check, types:check, trace, docs, formats and the focused vitest run over every touched suite are green, with one exception outside the phase: S30 of the standards suite spawns the machine's `vibe`, whose `install` refuses `--offline` on this machine, and the suite's only change here is one REUSE expectation. Deferrals: DEF-4 resolved, DEF-6 added (the owned roots as guard scopes). Judgment calls, each recorded in its fact: `annotate --own` refuses a path that narrows to nothing and a `--year` other than the profile's, and a CR-ended file about to be edited is `CK-E-CRLF`; `gen licensing` reports `owner` and `dryRun` in its `--json` data beyond the spec's list, and a bad or missing owner is `CK-E-CONFIG`.

Phases 1 and 3 landed as three commits (the design and this plan; the contract area `licensing` with the capability, the shape rules, the stub type's answer and the specifications of PROP-016/019/015/007/012/014 and FEAT-002 S91-S96; the editor family's answer with modules/vscode/PROP-010). Two findings on the way, both fixed in the engine before Phase 2: a restricted overlay target admitted additions of depth two only, so a manifest's scalar `license` key could not be set by an overlay - the target gained `allowedScalarKeys` (PROP-016 `TYPE-AREA-LAYERS`, PROP-005 `OVERLAY-NPM-DECLARED-TARGETS`), a guarded replacement with the pin's value as `expectUpstream`; and the package and CI engines still mapped `npm` to `npm.cmd` on Windows themselves, which the report then showed, while the spawn resolves a bare name since f3e8d8c - the mapping went, and `package` reports the words the type names. The block header is laid out as a carrier (the copyright line carries nothing after the holder; D4); `codkit.licensing.json` gained version 2 with the `product` block; the fixture upstream carries a `LICENSE` so the stub's component licence has a source at the pin.

Phase 0: the pilot measured (its repository, remotes, copies, fork tree and build), the engine's licensing machinery and the contract read, DESIGN-003 written with twelve decisions, this plan proposed. No tree change outside the two documents.
